articles.title: “Game-changer for our organization and the kids”: How Conor McGregor turned a UFC rivalry into a $500,000 lifeline for Louisiana kids after earning praise for COVID-19 relief
articles.summary: MMA News: Conor McGregor’s rivalry with Dustin Poirier ended up helping hundreds of Louisiana children. On April 26, 2021, McGregor’s team donated $500,000 to t.
articles.body: Conor McGregor’s rivalry with Dustin Poirier ended up helping hundreds of Louisiana children. On April 26, 2021, McGregor’s team donated $500,000 to the Boys & Girls Club of Acadiana. The move came after a public dispute over McGregor’s earlier pledge to Poirier’s foundation, but it also reflected the charitable work that had earned McGregor praise during the COVID-19 crisis.The donation gave the UFC star another chance to put his money behind a cause. This time, the money went straight towards helping children in southern Louisiana. How did Conor McGregor’s $500,000 donation become a win for Louisiana kids?Conor McGregor originally pledged $500,000 to Dustin Poirier’s Good Fight Foundation before their UFC 257 rematch on January 24, 2021. After Poirier won by TKO, the two fighters clashed on social media over the donation. McGregor said his team needed more details about how the money would be used.The situation took a different turn on April 26, when McGregor’s team sent the $500,000 to the Boys & Girls Club of Acadiana. Club president and CEO Missy Andrade told ESPN that a McGregor representative had called unexpectedly the previous week.The money had a clear purpose. The club planned to use it for an eight-week summer programme across six locations in southern Louisiana. Around 600 children stood to benefit, with the funding also supporting health and recreation programmes.Andrade explained the impact during her interview with ESPN.“It was totally unexpected, of course. Extremely appreciated and it's really a game-changer for our organization and the kids we have.”Poirier also backed the decision. During his ESPN interview with Ariel Helwani, he said helping people remained the main goal.“It wasn't a slap in the face. It was a high-five, because the people in the community are going to win.”That connection is crucial because McGregor had already shown a similar side during the pandemic. How did Conor McGregor earn praise for helping Ireland during COVID-19?In 2020, Conor McGregor turned his attention to Ireland as the COVID-19 crisis hit the country. Reports highlighted his donations of personal protective equipment to medical workers.By May 2020, McGregor had also personally delivered medical gowns to the Generation Health Medical Clinic in Dublin. The clinic’s medical director later described the surprise delivery as a major relief because the clinic had struggled to afford enough gowns.McGregor acknowledged the public praise on Twitter on July 2, 2020, after a supporter credited him for donating PPE across Ireland. He replied, “Thank you Sir 🙏.”The Louisiana donation came nearly a year later, but the idea stayed similar. McGregor used his resources to support people who needed help.The $500,000 did not erase the tension between McGregor and Poirier, but it gave the community something far more useful to take from it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UFC Hall of Famer makes color commentary debut at DWCS 91
articles.summary: Chris Weidman will test his chops on color commentary for the first time at Dana White's Contender Series 91.
articles.body:
Chris Weidman will continue to expand his horizons after retiring from MMA when he joins the commentary booth for the first time at Dana White's Contender Series 91 .

Weidman, a former UFC middleweight champion who was inducted into the Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class this summer, has found a post-career path for himself as a desk analyst on UFC broadcasts, as well as a co-host of Paramount's "Deep Waters" podcast alongside Dustin Poirier , Jorge Masvidal and Din Thomas.

Now Weidman will get the chance to call fights as part of Tuesday's DWCS 91 broadcast, a person with knowledge of the situation verified to MMA Junkie.

Weidman will join fellow color commentator Laura Sanko and play-by-play man Dan Hellie in the three-person commentary booth for the five-bout card from Meta APEX in Las Vegas ( Paramount+ ).

The 42-year-old Weidman (16-8 MMA, 12-8 UFC) last competed in MMA in December 2024, when he suffered a second-round TKO loss to Eryk Anders at UFC 310. The American is one of 14 fighters in UFC history to win an undisputed title with an undefeated record.

articles.title: Conor Benn reflects on Eubank Jr rivalry: ‘It was spiteful, it was personal’
articles.summary: On September 12 at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, NV, Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn will headline a co-promoted card between Zuffa Boxing and Golden Boy Promot...
articles.body:
On September 12 at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, NV, Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn will headline a co-promoted card between Zuffa Boxing and Golden Boy Promotions. Fight fans in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and most countries worldwide can catch the action live on DAZN pay-per-view and The Ultimate Tier, while the U.S. can watch the event on Paramount+ . Garcia-Benn will meet with Garcia's WBC welterweight title on the line.

In the build-up to September 12, Benn spoke to Dan Rafael , reflecting on why beating Eubank Jr was so personal.

Conor Benn prepares to challenge Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas

Despite never winning a world title, Benn (25-1, 14 KOs) is one of the biggest stars in the sport. Since returning to professional boxing after his much-publicised battles with PEDs, he has battled Eubank Jr twice, losing the first one, which was ultimately crowned the fight of the year. He has since left Matchroom, moving to Zuffa Boxing, where he has beaten Regis Prograis, before the fight with Garcia was announced.

Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) comes into the fight as the reigning WBC champ, a title he won against Mario Barrios. The American has often flattered to deceive during his career, but his talent is not in dispute. Garcia was electrifying against Devin Haney, but ultimately tested positive for the banned substance ostarine on both the day before and the day of the fight.

Conor Benn reflects on personal rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr

Speaking to Dan Rafael, Benn discussed his feelings around losing the first fight and winning the second, and why beating Eubank Jr was so personal:

"Because then if I had lost the second time around, it would have meant that he was really is better than me. I would have had to accept the fact that he is actually better than me. And because it was so personal…it was just personal. It was spiteful.

"It was real mixed feelings, even getting fight of the year. I lost, and I genuinely thought I'd knock him out. I lost to this guy, but I beat myself in there. I shouldn't have fought that fight in there, but the emotions were overwhelming."

articles.title: La UFC anuncia UFC 332... y pinta a uno de los peores eventos numerados de la historia
articles.standfirst: Wang Cong y Natalia Silva se jugarán el cinturón vacante de peso mosca en uno de los combates estelares más descafeinados que se recuerdan
articles.summary: Wang Cong y Natalia Silva se jugarán el cinturón vacante de peso mosca en uno de los combates estelares más descafeinados que se recuerdan
articles.body: Este pasado sábado, la UFC anunció en París el UFC 332 que se celebrará el próximo 3 de octubre en Salt Lake City, en lo que se espera que sea uno de los peores eventos numerados de la historia. El motivo no es otro que el combate estelar, donde Wang Cong (10-1) y Natalia Silva (20-5-1) se jugarán el cinturón vacante de peso mosca tras la lesión de Valentina Shevchenko. Con la desaparición de los PPV al inicio de año, esto puede sentar un precedente muy preocupante para la compañía. Desde hace unas semanas se rumoreaba que Valentina Shevchenko podría ser el combate estelar junto a Natalia Silva, algo que ya dejó mucho que desear a pesar de que 'Bullet' es una de las GOAT de las mma femeninas. Sin embargo, lo que nadie esperaba es que la peleadora kirguisa se lesionase los ligamentos del hombro y tuviese que dejar vacante el cinturón, lo que ha provocado que sea Cong quien la supla a pesar de ser la número seis de la división. Seguramente la UFC haya intentado buscar otro combate estelar de última hora, pero la mayoría de divisiones ya tienen peleas pactadas a futuro y el factor de la altura de Utah también ha sido un condicionante para que los grandes campeones de la promotora no quieran jugársela en corto aviso y sin apenas preparación. Con el nuevo acuerdo con Paramount, la UFC se ha separado del modelo de PPV, aunque hasta el momento no había realizado un evento numerado con un combate estelar tan poco mediático como este. Sin duda, el peor del año y uno de los peores que se recuerdan. Aún así, lo cierto es que el combate debería ser entretenido al enfrentar a dos strikers, y estará acompañado de varios enfrentamientos por los que merecerá la pena estar atentos a la cartelera. En la pelea co estelar, Payton Talbott (11-1) se enfrentará a Deiveson Figueiredo (25-7-1) con la intención de dar el salto definitivo a la parte alta del ránking de peso gallo, lo que le asentaría como una de las mayores superestrellas de la división gracias a su estilo y a su carisma. Además, Ateba Gautier (11-1) tendrá su primera prueba de fuego en la UFC al medirse a Roman Kopylov (15-5). Si le vence, demostrará que el hype es real y es un verdadero peligro para el peso medio. Otro de los combates del pueblo será el de King Green (36-17-1) contra Esteban Ribovics (16-3) en peso ligero, mientras que Roberto Soldic (21-4) debutará en la UFC ante Khaos Williams (16-5) con el cartel de doble campeón de KSW y un 91% de finalización. Imanol Rodríguez, Mick Parking, Damian Pinas... Muchos prospectos muy interesantes que compartirán cartelera y que permiten que el drama no sea mayor, aunque el combate estelar haya manchado todo lo anteriormente nombrado. No porque Cong y Silva Sean malas, ni mucho menos, sino porque una pelea estelar de un evento numerado debe ser mucho más que esto.

articles.title: Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash
articles.summary: A long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the proposed clash in November; Fury called out Oleksandr Usyk on Monday
articles.body:
With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent.

Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024.

Responding to Fury's comments in a statement given to Sky Sports News on Monday evening, Usyk's manager Sergey Lapin said: "Usyk is not Tyson's backup plan.

"If Fury needs an opponent, he should visit the Ready to Fight platform . They can help him find a worthy opponent there.

"Oleksandr is always open to big challenges. But serious intentions are backed by a concrete offer, not statements in the press."

Usyk announced in June that he was vacating the three heavyweight belts he still held at the time, but the 39-year-old said he was not yet retiring, and has recently been linked with a fight against Deontay Wilder.

Usyk, who holds a perfect 25-0 professional record, claimed successive wins over Joshua in 2021 and 2022, but has become part of the Brit's training team over the last year.

Both Joshua and Fury have signed individual contracts for what was slated to be a November contest, but have yet to agree on where the fight will take place, with speculation suggesting it could be held in New York City.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says he and his fighter want the contest to take place in London, while Fury says his rival is trying to avoid a bout that has been more than a decade in the making.

"This will only lead me to a fight with Oleksandr Usyk," Fury said in a video posted on Instagram .

"Oleksandr you're his [Joshua's] trainer and his sensei and you know he is weak minded... and that he would never fight the Gypsy King which you have had the guts to do twice.

"You got the decisions last time, fair play to you. Good luck to you, let's do it again. Let's run it back in November. The ball is now in your court... do you want to fight me this year, 2026, or are you calling it quits?

"Let me know because I am now looking for a new opponent."

articles.title: Josh Hokit plays matchmaker in the UFC heavyweight division
articles.summary: Josh Hokit has laid out his idea of perfect UFC matchmaking.
articles.body:
With all of the uncertainty disrupting the UFC heavyweight division at present, Josh Hokit isn't going to wait in limbo.

Fairly new to the promotion, Hokit has already made a splash just 10 months into his life with the UFC. The controversial All-American wrestler earned a spot in the octagon with a second-round stoppage victory on the Contender Series. Four fights later, with wins over Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis , the 28-year-old finds himself in the UFC title picture and a serious threat to each man ranked above him.

His relentless, fan-friendly style inside the cage is accompanied by an unserious, pro-wrestling-like approach to the sport, making him one of the most unique characters on the roster. But enough with the fun and games. Hokit is fed up with waiting for movement in his division and has decided to hit out at heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall .

"Eddie Hearn's strategy with Aspinall is obvious: stall with 'he'll fight when cleared' to buy time in contract negotiations. Back in June, Tom said he'd fight Gane Sept 6th. Now Eddie is talking out of his ass: "He's training, he's ready, he's eager to come back. You mean he didn't get medical clearance before starting full training months ago? Total [bullsh*t]."

Continuing his attack on his peers, Hokit then opted to play matchmaker.

"Nobody wants to see Alex get beat by Gane again. If UFC books me vs Alex, Eddie holds the UFC by the balls and drags negotiations out forever because I'm the ONLY viable fight left for Gane that brings real eyes," Hokit continued.

"I'm 10-0 (I've won all my fights at HW unlike low IQ, [Portuguese], Indian guy) and I put on a show. Ciryl and I need to find out who the best athlete in the UFC is. I'm the only man who can make him pay for being a dirty [piece of sh*t] and I won't need a year off or blame a ref."

"Incredible Hok vs. Ciryl Gane. Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira. Let's have a f***ing party at MSG."

articles.title: “I’m enjoying this”: Brandon Moreno keeps moving forward as the former champion prepares for a defining Noche UFC return
articles.summary: MMA News: Brandon Moreno has waited a long time for his Noche UFC moment. The former flyweight champion will finally compete at the event when he faces Joseph M.
articles.body: Brandon Moreno has waited a long time for his Noche UFC moment. The former flyweight champion will finally compete at the event when he faces Joseph Morales on Sept. 12 in Glendale, Arizona. The timing carries extra weight after two straight losses, but Moreno is not allowing those setbacks to take away from what still matters most to him: fighting, training and enjoying the sport.Brandon Moreno keeps moving forward as his long-awaited Noche UFC return finally becomes a realityMoreno's first Noche UFC appearance has been a long time coming. The Tijuana native missed the first three editions because of scheduling issues and minor injuries, but this year he made the event a priority.He did not have a particular opponent in mind. Moreno simply wanted to make sure he would be healthy and available when Noche UFC arrived."Hey, just offer me a fight. I don't care who, and I'll be ready."That approach eventually led him to Morales, a fighter whose career path has some similarities to Moreno's own.Morales was previously released by the UFC before rebuilding his career and winning The Ultimate Fighter. He returned to the promotion and has won his first two fights since coming back, giving him plenty of confidence heading into one of the biggest opportunities of his career.Moreno knows that motivation could make Morales especially dangerous."Joseph Morales has an interesting history, because he has a similar history to me. He was in the UFC then he got released, and he had to get some victories. He won 'The Ultimate Fighter,' he came back, right now he's 2-0, so he's super dangerous because he's motivated."For Moreno, the fight also brings him back to Glendale, a place tied to one of the biggest moments of his career. It was there that he first captured the flyweight championship at UFC 263, making his return to the area especially meaningful.Brandon Moreno turns the page on two losses as he fights to begin a new chapter at Noche UFCMoreno enters Noche UFC after losses to Tatsuro Taira and Lone'er Kavanagh. Another defeat would give him the first three-fight losing streak of his career, adding significant pressure to an already important matchup.Still, Moreno does not appear interested in getting trapped by what happened in his last two fights."I just want to win, brother. I'm fighting because I still feel super good at the gym, feel super good in my practices, my sparring looks super sharp."That belief could be crucial as Moreno attempts to regain his place among the division's leading fighters. His recent results have changed the conversation around him, but his championship experience and years competing at the highest level remain important parts of his story.More than anything, Moreno wants to stay present rather than worry about what another loss could mean."I'm still enjoying this. I'm still enjoying the game, enjoying waking up every morning to prepare myself to go to the gym, and that's it. I'm super focused on the present."His words offer a different perspective on a fighter entering a difficult stretch. Moreno is not pretending the losses did not happen. Instead, he is choosing to focus on the part of the sport that continues to give him a reason to train every morning.That makes his Noche UFC return about more than simply getting another win. A victory over Morales could help rebuild his momentum, but the fight also gives Moreno a chance to remind fans that his story is far from finished.For a former champion who has already experienced the highest point of the sport, this next chapter may be about proving that setbacks do not have to be the ending.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alex Pereira Ready to Leave UFC Freedom 250 Controversy Behind for Ciryl Gane Rematch
articles.summary: Alex Pereira recently addressed UFC fans about his comeback and is ready to rematch Ciryl Gane in his potential return outing.
articles.body:
It has been nearly three months since Alex Pereira's bid to become a UFC champion in a third weight class came to a brutal halt at UFC Freedom 250. Ciryl Gane delivered a statement-making performance to score a second-round knockout in the historic White House co-main event.

The win was a huge moment for Gane, who became just the second fighter in UFC history to win two interim titles in the same division. More importantly, it put the French heavyweight in line for a highly anticipated rematch with undisputed champion Tom Aspinall.

However, much of the post-fight discussion wasn't about Gane's performance. Instead, the spotlight quickly turned to the 11 finishing shots he landed on Pereira, with seven appearing to connect to the back of the head and being deemed illegal.

Pereira has since repeatedly called out referee Herb Dean and even demanded that he be removed from officiating his future fights. So far, though, nothing has changed on that front, and it appears Pereira is ready to put the controversy behind him and focus on what comes next.

The Brazilian had previously talked about returning in November at Madison Square Garden, with the event now set as UFC 334 on November 14. "Poatan" had planned to fight the winner of the interim title fight between Gane and Aspinall, but it appears he now has someone else in mind.

And unsurprisingly, it's Gane. In a new video posted to Instagram, Pereira made it clear that he wants another crack at the Frenchman.

He said, "After much time, after resting what I needed to do, after much work, after my last fight, many people are talking with who will Alex fight? I'm seeing many opinions, but I think the fight that makes sense is Ciryl Gane."

He added, "That's the fight. I'm going to work on that and from what I'm seeing, it's something that's going to happen. How the last fight [ended], there were illegal shots. I think now, with another opportunity, I can come back and show what I can do, what I can achieve, which is the third belt. I'm very excited for that, and I'll work for that. Chama!"

Interestingly, that lines up with Gane's own stance on his next fight . The Frenchman recently said that he should face Aspinall if the champion is able to return in time, but a rematch with Pereira could also be on the table.

The biggest roadblock right now is Aspinall's health. The Englishman has been out of action for nearly 11 months after accidental eye pokes from Gane forced their first meeting at UFC 321 to end in a no-contest. Aspinall has since undergone several more tests as he continues working toward a full recovery.

If the champion isn't ready to return soon, Gane could potentially take another fight in the meantime. That could open the door for Pereira to get his rematch before the end of 2026.

And if the UFC does go that route, the second meeting between Pereira and Gane could be even bigger than the first. With more at stake, the Brazilian's pursuit of a historic third UFC title would give the rematch plenty of intrigue, and potentially make it one of the biggest heavyweight fights of the year.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: Date, ringwalk, UK time, undercard, venue, records & how to follow on the BBC
articles.summary: All you need to know about Ryan Garcia's WBC welterweight title defence against Conor Benn in Las Vegas on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Conor Benn will attempt to emulate his father Nigel by winning a world title when he faces WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas on Saturday.

After a blockbuster 2025, in which Benn lost to Chris Eubank Jr before beating his bitter rival in the middleweight rematch, the 29-year-old returns to welterweight in pursuit of world honours.

American Garcia won the WBC belt in February with a hard-fought unanimous decision victory over Mario Barrios.

The 28-year-old, who has a record of 25 wins, two defeats and one no-contest, has home advantage with the bout taking place at Vegas' T-Mobile Arena.

Will Garcia come through his first defence successfully? Or can Benn spring a surprise?

Here is all you need to know about Garcia v Benn.

Live text commentary on the BBC Sport website and app will begin at 03:00 BST on Sunday, 13 September.

Garcia and Benn are not scheduled to make their ringwalks before 04:00 .

All timings are estimated and subject to change.

Ryan Garcia (c) v Conor Benn - WBC welterweight world title

Jai Opetaia (c) v Noel Mikaelian - Zuffa cruiserweight title

Damazion Vanhouter v Raphael Akpejiori - heavyweight

Mark Magsayo v Andres Cortes - lightweight

How do Garcia and Benn's records compare?

Garcia won 15 national amateur titles before turning professional in 2016 and earning a first-round TKO victory on his debut.

He began his career as a lightweight but also featured at super-featherweight as he stitched together a 20-fight win streak.

Garcia beat Briton Luke Campbell by seventh-round TKO to win the interim WBC lightweight title.

His first career loss came in his 24th bout when he was stopped in round seven by fellow American Gervonta Davis.

In 2024, Garcia was handed a shot at WBC light-welterweight champion Devin Haney but he missed weight and was not eligible to claim the belt after picking up a decision victory.

That result was later overturned to a no-contest; Garcia was also handed a one-year suspension after failing a drugs test.

Garcia lost to Rolly Romero on his return in May 2025 but bounced back with a decision win over Barrios in February to claim his first world title.

Like Garcia, Benn turned professional in 2016 and enjoyed a similarly stunning start to his career, winning his first 23 fights.

In 2023, he was also suspended from boxing for failing two voluntary drugs tests.

His ban was lifted by the National Anti-Doping Panel, although he remained suspended by the UK Anti-Doping Agency (Ukad) and was unable to fight in the UK.

He fought twice in the United States - beating Rodolfo Orozco and Peter Dobson - before his ban was eventually lifted following a two-year battle with Ukad and the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC).

Benn's first fight back in the UK ended in defeat against Eubank in April 2025, but he avenged what remains his sole career loss seven months later.

What belts are on the line for Garcia v Benn?

Garcia makes the first defence of his WBC welterweight title.

It is the first time Benn, who is ranked number one by the WBC, will compete for a world title.

Teofimo Lopez holds the WBA belt, with Liam Paro in possession of the IBF title and Devin Haney reigning as WBO champion.

articles.title: UFC: Alex Pereira calls for Ciryl Gane rematch as next fight
articles.summary: UFC star Alex Pereira insists the fight that makes the most sense for him is a rematch against Ciryl Gane.
articles.body:
Alex Pereira has insisted he wants to fight Ciryl Gane next after being knocked out by the Frenchman in their interim heavyweight UFC title fight last June.

Pereira, 39, was stopped by Gane in his bid to become the first three-weight champion in the UFC.

Speaking on social media, Pereira said that after a period of rest, he expected to get a rematch with the 36-year-old.

"I'm seeing many opinions but I think the fight that makes sense is Ciryl Gane," he said.

"That's the fight. I'm going to work on that and from what I'm seeing, it's something that's going to happen.

"How the last fight [ended], there were illegal shots. I think now with another opportunity I can come back and show what I can do, what I can achieve, which is the third belt.

"I'm very excited for that and I'll work for that."

Gane should fight UFC champion Tom Aspinall in what would be an undisputed contest next, but the Briton is still recovering from eye injuries sustained in his own fight against Gane almost a year ago.

Aspinall's return date is unknown but he has been cleared to return to training and insisted he has no plans to leave the UFC or retire.

Should Aspinall be forced to sit out the rest of 2026, Gane may well take another bout in his absence.

How bullying led Britain's Campbell to the UFC

Pereira was unhappy with Gane's tactics in their fight, suggesting several of his heaviest blows were illegal strikes to the back of his head, something his opponent denied.

Gane is in his second spell as interim heavyweight champion and has twice been beaten in fights for the full title.

Brazil's Pereira has been UFC champion at middleweight and light-heavyweight and achieved that feat in just seven fights, the fastest run to two-division champion status in UFC history.

Michael 'Venom' Page has been removed from the UFC rankings after fighting out his contract at UFC Paris on Saturday.

The Briton's lacklustre decision victory over Nursulton Ruziboev was booed by fans inside Accor Arena, with Page landing just 12 significant strikes through three rounds.

Page said he hoped to reach a new deal with the UFC but American journalist John Morgan , external confirmed media were instructed to remove him from their ranking considerations, an indicator he is not renewing with the MMA promotion.

The 39-year-old holds a 5-1 record in the UFC, but has failed to produce the eye-catching knockout performances he is known for.

Posting on his Instagram on Monday, Page gave little away about his immediate future.

"Thank you Paris for having me. I'm grateful for the support you gave me," he said.

"Stepping in the cage is a privilege I do not take for granted and I look forward to bigger challenges."

articles.summary: Original The Ultimate Fighter middleweight tournament winner Diego Sanchez has been arrested, again. In July 2025, Sanchez was arrested in New Mexico on gun...
articles.body:
Original The Ultimate Fighter middleweight tournament winner Diego Sanchez has been arrested, again.

In July 2025, Sanchez was arrested in New Mexico on gun charges after firing a gun from a moving vehicle. In May, he received five years of probation over the incident … probation he violated when he was arrested in Socorro, New Mexico on Monday afternoon (Sept. 7, 2026) for aggravated driving under the influence.

Other than the aggravated DUI and probation violation charges, there's no further information on Sanchez's arrest at this time.

Diego Sanchez was one of the UFC's biggest stars during the promotion's turnaround from financial destitution to MMA mega-power. As UFC CEO Dana White has told the story many times, the promotion was over $40 million in the red when they paid Spike TV to air The Ultimate Fighter, which became a massive success. Diego Sanchez was one of Season 1's champions and went on to have an extensive career in the UFC from 2005 to 2020.

Diego was always a bit of an odd duck, but no one could anticipate the way his UFC career would end. After years of being trained at Jackson Wink in Albuquerque, Sanchez allowed an unknown life coach named Joshua Fabia to become his manager and trainer. Video of Fabia chasing his students with a knife and punching a suspended Sanchez in the head repeatedly led many to question Fabia's methods.

Sanchez would end up being released by the UFC after Fabia requested all of Diego Sanchez's medical records from the promotion, which Sanchez later admitted was a prelude to an attempted lawsuit to sue to UFC for allowing him to fight after he was showing symptoms of CTE.

A Dark Side of the Cage episode by Vice TV details how Sanchez thought "this guy was gonna kill me or I was gonna have to kill him" in order to escape the toxic relationship. In the end, Sanchez would pay Fabia $100,000 to leave. The same show touched on Sanchez's issues with drugs and alcohol … issues it seems still persist to this day based on his most recent arrest.

articles.title: “It made me who I am today”: How Conor McGregor turned his childhood roots into a $600 million whiskey empire before losing control of Proper No. Twelve
articles.summary: MMA News: Conor McGregor built Proper No. Twelve around the place that shaped his early life. When he launched the Irish whiskey on Sept. 17 2018 he named it af.
articles.body: Conor McGregor built Proper No. Twelve around the place that shaped his early life. When he launched the Irish whiskey on Sept. 17 2018 he named it after Dublin 12 where he grew up in Crumlin and learned to fight. What started as a personal connection to his childhood soon became a major business venture that reached a deal worth up to $600 million before McGregor eventually lost control of the brand.The story is more complicated than a famous fighter putting his name on a bottle. McGregor connected the whiskey directly to his upbringing and spent time developing the product before taking it to the market. Proper No. Twelve later became a major part of his business portfolio but its ownership changed significantly before the brand moved forward without his name and likeness. Conor McGregor turned his Dublin 12 childhood into the identity of Proper No. TwelveWhen Conor McGregor launched Proper No. Twelve in September 2018 he explained that the name came directly from the area where he grew up. In the official launch statement released on Sept. 2018 he said: “I come from a place called Crumlin in Dublin 12. It’s a place dear to my heart. It’s where I learned how to fight; it made me who I am today.” That statement gave the number on the bottle a personal meaning because Dublin 12 represented both his childhood and the beginning of his fighting journey.McGregor also connected his upbringing with the values he wanted the business to represent. In the same launch material he said: “Growing up on the streets of Dublin 12 I learned the values of loyalty and hard work.” He added that he was entering the Irish whiskey market “with passion and with purpose.” Those comments made it clear that McGregor wanted the brand story to come from his own background rather than simply using his UFC fame to sell an unrelated product.The product itself also went through a development process before the launch. McGregor worked with David Elder who had experience with Guinness and later worked at the Old Bushmills Distillery. The team reportedly tested close to 100 blends before selecting the whiskey that became Proper No. Twelve. McGregor described the process in 2018 by saying: “We created close to one hundred blends and ultimately selected what we knew was the one and only proper whiskey blend.”That approach helped McGregor position Proper No. Twelve as more than a celebrity endorsement. His name brought attention to the product but the brand also had a clear story behind its name and a development process that involved experienced whiskey professionals. The timing also worked in his favour because McGregor had already built a huge international following through his UFC career and could promote the whiskey directly to that audience.Conor McGregor built Proper No. Twelve into a $600 million business before losing controlThe biggest business development came on April 27 2021 when Proximo Spirits acquired a majority stake in Proper No. Twelve in a transaction valued at up to $600 million. Proximo already owned 49% of the company and the reported figure included $250 million that McGregor and his partners had earned during the brand's first two years with the spirits company. The deal showed how far Proper No. Twelve had moved from its 2018 launch and turned McGregor's personal whiskey project into a valuable commercial brand.McGregor did not immediately disappear from the business after that transaction. He retained an interest and continued to promote Proper No. Twelve as its brand ambassador. At that stage he remained closely associated with the whiskey and continued using his profile to keep the product in front of consumers. The situation changed later when Proximo increased its ownership and eventually took complete control of the company.In November 2024 Proximo confirmed that it had become the 100% owner of Proper No. Twelve and said: “Going forward we do not plan to use Mr McGregor’s name and likeness in the marketing of the brand.” The statement marked a major change because the whiskey had originally used McGregor's childhood connection to Dublin 12 as one of its central selling points.That decision came shortly after an Irish High Court jury found McGregor liable in a civil case brought by Nikita Hand in November 2024. McGregor denied the allegation and said he planned to appeal. Proximo did not state that the court case caused its decision to stop using McGregor's name and likeness. The company simply confirmed that its future marketing would move ahead without him.The Proper No. Twelve story then gained another legal chapter in 2026 when former teammate Artem Lobov pursued a claim against McGregor over the whiskey business. Lobov alleged that McGregor had promised him a 5% share of the proceeds from the sale and argued that he had played an important role in the brand's creation. McGregor denied that such an agreement existed while acknowledging that he had offered Lobov $1 million for his work on the whiskey project. Lobov rejected that offer and continued his legal claim.The dispute ended on April 15 2026 when McGregor and Lobov reached a confidential settlement before the case went to trial. The terms were not made public. The settlement closed another chapter in a business story that began with McGregor looking back at his childhood neighbourhood and eventually became a multimillion-dollar whiskey venture.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is less and less likely to happen, says Johnny Nelson
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's all-British blockbuster fight has been stuck in negotiations in recent months, but Eddie Hearn revealed last week that talks have 'reopened' to stage the fight at Wembley
articles.body:
Promoter Eddie Hearn has stated that Joshua signed a contract to fight Fury at Wembley amid an ongoing dispute over the location of the fight, with Madison Square Garden in New York also being considered as a potential venue.

Nelson believes Joshua and his team are even more determined to get the fight entirely on their terms after the unified champion displayed his vulnerabilities while being floored twice in his comeback win over Kristian Prenga .

"No, I don't [think Fury vs Joshua will happen]," Nelson told Sky Sports.

"Unless the other side decides to lay down and say: 'You know what, we'll give you what you want'. No, I don't.

"I think Anthony Joshua and [his promotional team] Matchroom Boxing have every reason to stand their ground.

"Firstly, because you look at Anthony Joshua's last performance; that doesn't fill you with confidence.

"Secondly, because they've signed a contract and so, if they're going to embark on this fight, they're going to say: 'This is what we asked for; if you don't want to do it, that's a you problem'."

Hearn has revealed that he held fresh talks with London Mayor Sadiq Khan in a bid to ensure the two Brits fight in front of a home crowd, despite concerns over a later curfew for Wembley Stadium.

But Nelson believes Joshua and his team's insistence that the terms of the contract should be followed could mean the bout is not agreed.

"I think it's less and less likely to happen," said Nelson.

"They have put the pressure on. Sadiq Khan has got involved, and he's said: 'We're going to do everything possible to make this happen and bring this business to the UK'.

"Anthony Joshua has said to Eddie Hearn, 'We've got a contract; stick to the contract. No nudging; this is what we're doing.

"Unless Turki Alalshikh [who is organising the fight] and Tyson [Fury], say: 'All right, let's do this.'

"I think that the chance of the fight happening is less and less.

"If I were Team AJ, I'd do the same, because AJ's performance didn't fill me with complete and utter belief that this will go our way.

"I'm quite sure if it was the other way around and Tyson Fury was the one who performed as AJ did in his last fight, even though he fought the night before, I'm quite sure this wouldn't be as much of an issue.

articles.title: Una de las grandes voces de la UFC cree que el Gaethje vs Topuria 2 es posible
articles.standfirst: Jon Anik, comentarista principal de los grandes eventos, ha revelado que está habiendo conversaciones internas para llevar la pelea a cabo
articles.summary: Jon Anik, comentarista principal de los grandes eventos, ha revelado que está habiendo conversaciones internas para llevar la pelea a cabo
articles.body: El pasado 14 de junio, Ilia Topuria perdió su récord invicto y su cinturón de peso ligero en el UFC Casa Blanca ante Justin Gaethje. Desde entonces, el peleador estadounidense ha repetido por activa y por pasiva que no cree que 'El Matador' se merezca una revancha al considerar que le superó con creces y no tenía ninguna defensa de cinturón en esta categoría. Sin embargo, Jon Anik -comentarista principal de la UFC y una de las voces más autorizadas- ha revelado que está habiendo conversaciones internas al respecto para un futuro. No hay que olvidar que Topuria venía de noquear de manera consecutiva a tres leyendas de la talla de Alexander Volkanovski, Max Holloway -nadie le había noqueado- y Charles Oliveira. Consiguió destronar al GOAT de peso pluma, subió a peso ligero y se convirtió en el primer doble campeón invicto de la historia de la UFC. Además, tanto Holloway como Oliveira habían finalizado a Gaethje con anterioridad, por lo que se puede considerar que lo que pasó en la Casa Blanca hace poco menos de tres meses fue simplemente una mala noche. Topuria ha hecho méritos suficientes para recibir esa revancha, y por la superestrella que es para la UFC sería un movimiento lógico pensando en el negocio. De hecho, según Anik es lo que se está planteando. "Creo que hay conversaciones internas para intentar organizar una revancha entre Gaethje y Topuria. Sería un combate absolutamente enorme y, según mis predicciones, eso es lo que va a suceder", afirmó en su propio podcast. Gaethje llegó a reconocer hace unos meses que en el momento en el que perda se retirará. Con 37 años, el único sueño que le quedaba por cumplir en su carrera era ser campeón indiscutido, y ya lo tiene. Por tanto, ahora intentará realizar una o dos defensas y decir adiós por todo lo alto, con el riesgo que eso conlleva. Ilia quiere tener esa oportunidad de redimirse de su única derrota profesional ante Justin, por lo que la UFc le haría un gran favor si cierra ese enfrentamiento. En caso de darse esta pelea, lo que está claro es que no ocurrirá hasta 2027. Había ciertos rumores de que Ilia podía volver a finales de año, pero en su reciente comunicado reveló que además de las fracturas de los dos orbitales y la nariz también tenía una en el pie. 'The Highlight', por su parte, ya ha dicho que no tiene pensado competir más en 2026. Este año ha conseguido el cinturón interino, el indiscutido y el especial de la Casa Blanca, así que ahora le toca descansar y disfrutar de ello. Lo ideal para 'El Matador' es que la UFC meta presión a Justin y se cierre esta revancha, ya que si logra ganarla para su discurso sería perfecto. Una mala noche que habría vengado como solo los mejores saben, y que le permitiría continuar "invicto" moralmente como ya pasó en otros casos como Georges St-Pierre con Matt Serra. De momento, tocará esperar varios meses hasta que se conozcan noticias de primera mano.

articles.title: Diego Sanchez Arrested on Aggravated DWI While Serving Alcohol-Free Probation
articles.summary: Diego Sanchez is back in custody in New Mexico only months after avoiding prison in a felony gun case. The retired UFC fighter was arrested... Read More
articles.body:
Diego Sanchez is back in custody in New Mexico only months after avoiding prison in a felony gun case.

The retired UFC fighter was arrested Monday, September 7, by Socorro City Police and booked into the Socorro County Jail. Booking information lists aggravated driving while intoxicated and a probation violation, according to TMZ .

The new alcohol allegation comes while Sanchez is serving five years of supervised probation stemming from a 2025 case in which he pleaded guilty to shooting from a motor vehicle. One of the conditions attached to his supervision bars him from using alcohol.

Sanchez avoided prison when the gun case was resolved earlier this year after prosecutors had asked the judge to incarcerate him. The September arrest now leaves him facing the new DWI allegation as well as a reported violation of the probation that kept him out of prison.

Records List an Alcohol Concentration Above .16

Sanchez, 44, was booked at approximately 5:17 p.m. Monday. Court and booking information reviewed by MMA Fighting lists an alcohol concentration greater than .16 in connection with the aggravated DWI allegation.

New Mexico law defines aggravated DWI to include driving with an alcohol concentration of .16 or higher within three hours of driving when the alcohol was consumed before or while operating the vehicle. The threshold is twice the state's standard .08 limit for adult drivers.

The first reports did not explain why officers encountered Sanchez, where he was reportedly driving, what type of chemical test produced the listed alcohol concentration or whether anyone else was in the vehicle. No crash or injury connected with the arrest had been reported when the initial accounts were published, and Sanchez has not been convicted of the new allegations.

Sanchez Avoided Prison in His 2025 Gun Case

The probation stems from Sanchez's July 2025 arrest in Albuquerque. Police said he was riding in the passenger seat of a Jeep traveling past a crash scene near Interstate 40 and University Boulevard when he fired a gun from the vehicle. No one was injured.

Sanchez initially denied firing the weapon, but he later pleaded guilty in February 2026 to a fourth-degree felony charge of shooting at or from a motor vehicle. ESPN reported that prosecutors sought two years in prison when he was sentenced in March.

The judge instead imposed five years of supervised probation and 800 hours of community service. KOB reported that Sanchez told the court he had been working on sobriety and treatment before sentencing. Conditions imposed during the earlier case included restrictions on alcohol and drugs, and the new booking lists a probation violation alongside the aggravated DWI allegation.

The New Arrest Could Put His Probation at Risk

Probation allows Sanchez to serve his sentence in the community as long as he follows the conditions imposed by the court and supervision authorities. KOB reported after his March sentencing that violations could expose him to incarceration, although what action will be taken after the new arrest will be decided through the court and probation process.

The arrest comes years after Sanchez's run as one of the UFC's best-known fighters. He won the first season of The Ultimate Fighter in 2005, challenged B.J. Penn for the UFC lightweight championship in 2009 and later saw his 2009 fight against Clay Guida inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame's Fight Wing.

Sanchez's final UFC appearance came in 2020. He later returned to competition outside the promotion, including an MMA bout in 2022 and a bare-knuckle boxing match against Austin Trout in 2023.

As of MMA Fighting's September 8 report, Sanchez remained in the Socorro County Jail and no bond had been set. The aggravated DWI and probation violation allegations now proceed while his five-year supervised probation from the gun case remains in effect.

articles.title: Salahdine Parnasse wants 'war' with Max Holloway after UFC Paris debut, has no interest in taking it slow
articles.summary: Parnasse officially arrived as a lightweight contender at UFC Paris this past Saturday.
articles.body:
Salahdine Parnasse officially arrived as a lightweight contender at UFC Paris this past Saturday . And after a stellar performance in his much-anticipated promotional debut, the former KSW two-division champion already knows who he wants next.

Tasked with veteran lightweight contender Dan Hooker in Saturday's main event, Parnasse (24-2) only needed minutes to put away "Hangman" with a vicious body kick. Speaking on Tuesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show," Parnasse expressed how eager he is to fight again. If the Frenchman had his way, he'd go again tomorrow after taking no damage against Hooker and instantly returning to training on Monday.

Parnasse, 28, said he's eying at least one more fight in 2026 — and sitting squarely in his crosshairs is the former BMF and featherweight champion, Max Holloway.

"It could be good for Max Holloway to accept the fight, because Max, he really likes challenges," Parnasse told Uncrowned through an interpreter. "And Max knows that I'm a very, very good fighter, and we can do very good work together. So I think that it could be a very, very good fight and a very good war. Max really likes that, and also, I think he is very humble.

"This fight will be with a lot of respect because I respect Max a lot."

After the anticlimactic scenes of Holloway's rematch with Conor McGregor in July , the all-time great featherweight-turned-lightweight contender seems content waiting on the sidelines until a McGregor trilogy fight is possible in 2027. In the case that Parnasse can't land the big fish that is Hawaii's finest, he just wants someone ranked in the top five.

"I can fight anyone. I'm ready for anyone in the top five," Parnasse said. "I really want to get to the top five. Right now, Max Holloway would be the perfect fight for me."

Prior to his seemingly inevitable arrival in the UFC, Parnasse was a force on MMA's European scene, capturing two titles with Poland's KSW promotion and establishing himself as one of the most talented lightweights in the entire world. The latest win over Hooker extended Parnasse's win streak to six, but despite his great success outside of the Octagon, a fair bit of skepticism still existed ahead of UFC Paris about whether or not he was ready for the sport's biggest stage.

In Parnasse's fight before Paris, he made his debut on U.S. soil with an impressive first-round finish of Kenneth Cross on Netflix's MVP MMA event this past May .

Between that, as well as his impressive run through KSW, Parnasse believed the time was finally perfect for his UFC run to begin.

"I really think it was good timing for me," Parnasse said. "There's a new generation coming into the UFC, and I really think it was a good time to have some new challenges to maybe get the belt one day with this new generation."

As for the critics, Parnasse believes there isn't much left to silence. His performances have spoken for themselves, and he's ready to keep making noise with his actions en route to an eventual title opportunity.

"I really, really think that I'm ready, and I trained for a long time for that — since I was 11 years old. I was very ready for that," Parnasse said.

"I did three fights before the belt in the KSW against the big names in KSW. I did a great fight, and for the UFC, I don't know what's going to happen. I called out for Max Holloway. I really hope that he's going to accept, but I want to follow my manager and see what's going to happen."

articles.body:
Rising UFC heavyweight and former NFL player Anthony Wint is racking up the fights.

Team USA has finished the group phase with an impressive unbeaten run. Apart from an upset scare against Italy, the other two wins were commanding team efforts.

USA won 94-61 against China on Friday in the first game, 55-52 against Italy on Sunday, and 105-64 against Czech Republic on Monday. They will face Hungary in the quarterfinals on Thursday.

While the team's success has created a lot of excitement, one thing that might affect Team USA's viewership in the first knockout game of the World Cup is the tip off time. The game starts at 5:30 AM ET on Thursday, and fans were not sure if they would wake up to watch it.

The winner of tonight's game between Italy and Australia will face Spain in the quarterfinals. The winner of that game will face USA if they win against Hungary tomorrow.

Team USA bounce back in commanding fashion

After a close call vs Italy, USA got back to dominating. They won 105-64. Breanna Stewart led them with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Veterans Jackie Young and Napheesa Collier both added 12 points each.

The young trio of Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers also contributed in the win. Clark scored 9 points and had seven assists. Reese had 13 points and six rebounds. Bueckers scored 10 points and gave 5 assists.

articles.title: Gonezo! White Confirms MVP Release
articles.summary: Michael Page has competed inside the Octagon for the final time. In the final fight of his UFC contract, Page defeated Nursulton Ruziboev last weekend in Par...
articles.body:
Michael Page has competed inside the Octagon for the final time.

In the final fight of his UFC contract, Page defeated Nursulton Ruziboev last weekend in Paris in yet another boo birds. Despite promises of increased aggression , "MVP" landed just a dozen significant strikes in 15 full minutes of combat. One of those shots was a low kick that tore apart Ruziboev's knee at roughly the six minute mark … and Page still didn't increase his aggression.

As such, few were surprised when Page was suddenly ineligible for a UFC ranking . However, Page's free agency wasn't official until UFC CEO Dana White confirmed that the promotion would not be signing him while talking with media in the aftermath of Tuesday's Contender Series episode .

"That was his last fight on his contract," White explained. "I don't think we're re-signing him, no. What's the confusion? I think it's been pretty clear that he wasn't being re-signed, and that he would be taken out of the rankings because he's no longer on the roster."

Page's release is at least mildly controversial. On one hand, his recent fights have been fairly dreadful to watch, as Page has failed to push his advantage in punishingly low output performances. At the same time, Page did establish himself as a Top 15 (at least!) fighter in two different divisions while winning five of six of his Octagon bouts. UFC opting not to re-sign Page is a reminder that the promotion is focused more on entertainment than pure sport .

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Ryan Garcia skips first face-off with Conor Benn in Las Vegas
articles.summary: Conor Benn said Ryan Garcia "bottled" their first face-off after the American failed to turn up to their meeting on Tuesday in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia was a no-show for his first face-off with Conor Benn on Tuesday before their world title fight this weekend in Las Vegas.

The American was scheduled to attend a photo opportunity, but skipped it to leave Benn appearing alone.

Benn, 29, did have the company of his father, boxing legend Nigel Benn, who pretended to face off with his son.

After joking around with his dad, Benn said Garcia "didn't turn up".

"I apologise for Ryan doing what Ryan does and bottling it. We turn up, we're here, ready for the face-off," he said.

Garcia defends his WBC welterweight title at the T-Mobile Arena in Benn's first world championship bout.

The 28-year-old is the favourite for the contest and after failing to attend the first face-off of fight week, Garcia mocked Benn on Instagram.

"Nice relaxing time as Conor wastes time showing up to a face-off," he said.

"Back to the sauna you go, sausage getting cooked every way."

They are due to meet twice before fight night with the news conference on Thursday and the weigh-in on Friday.

Much has been made of Benn's weight cut for this contest, with the Briton having not fought at 10st 7lb (67kg) since 2022.

Benn had two fights with Chris Eubank Jr at middleweight before a 10st 12lb (69kg) catchweight against Regis Prograis in April.

Garcia has fought at lightweight and light-welterweight – missing weight for his light-welterweight contest against Devin Haney in 2024 – but is not expected to have issues with the weight, while Benn has said he does not intend to stay long at welterweight.

King tries to stop Mikaelian v Opetaia bout

In the co-main event on Saturday, Jai Opetaia is fighting Noel Mikaelian in a cruiserweight bout.

Mikaelian is the WBC champion, but could be stripped of the belt after withdrawing from his bout against the mandatory challenger in favour of facing the Australian.

Saturday's fight is further complicated by promoter Don King, who claims he has an exclusive deal with Mikaelian.

The veteran American promoter has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Zuffa Boxing and demanded the fight be cancelled.

Confirming Zuffa Boxing had received the legal letter, Dana White insisted the bout would be going ahead as planned.

"[Jai's] fighting this weekend," White said on Tuesday.

"I've always had good dealings with Don (King). When have you ever seen a scenario with us where we go and try to interfere with someone's contract?

articles.title: Imavov confirma que peleará ante Sean Strickland por el cinturón de peso medio
articles.standfirst: El peleador francés reveló lo que era un secreto a voces, por lo que solo falta saber la fecha para el enfrentamiento
articles.summary: El peleador francés reveló lo que era un secreto a voces, por lo que solo falta saber la fecha para el enfrentamiento
articles.body: Sean Strickland protagonizó una de las mayores sorpresas del año el pasado mayo al imponerse por decisión a Khamzat Chimaev en el UFC 329 y arrebatarle el cinturón de peso medio -ademas del invicto-. De esta forma, el peleador estadounidense recuperó la corona más de dos años después, y ahora se ha sabido que la primera defensa de su nuevo reinado será ante Nassourdine Imavov, tal y como ha confirmado el propio peleador francés. En un principio todo hacia indicar que la compañía enfrentaría a Chimaev y Strickland en una revancha por todo lo que significa el peleador checheno para la empresa, pero no parece haber gustado la rivalidad ficticia que montaron ambos para acabar abrazándose tras la pelea. Además, Imavov llevaba demasiado tiempo esperando su momento, y parece ser que finalmente le darán la oportunidad. "Sé la fecha desde hace tiempo", le comentaba Imavov al equipo de RMC Sport durante el UFC París del pasado sábado. Se espera que sea antes de que acabe el año, mientras que Chimaev apunta a enfrentarse a Caio Borralho en un combate que podría definir al siguiente retador al título. Esta oportunidad es la más importante de la carrera de un Imavov que se ha sabido reinventar dentro de la UFC, y que ha ganado cinco combates seguidos noqueando a Israel Adesanya o a Jared Canonnier entre otros. Además, ya sabe lo que es enfrentarse al estadounidense hace tres años. En aquella ocasión, la pelea también se realizó a cinco asaltos y Strickland fue el vencedor por decisión unánime. Sin embargo, desde entonces las cosas han cambiado mucho para ambos. En el caso de Sean, dos combates después superó a Adesanya para convertirse campeón indiscutido por primera vez, y ha seguido agrandando su legado con otra victoria ante Chimaev que le consagra como uno de los mejores peleadores de la historia de la división. Imavov aprendió mucho de aquella derrota, y su striking es uno de los más técnicos de la categoría. De hecho, será un choque de estilos entre los jabs, el cabecero y las patadas frontales de Strickland y la precisión de Nassourdine, que sabe que si consigue ganar al estadounidense podría ser el siguiente en medirse a Chimaev en otro de los combates más esperados de las 185 libras.

articles.title: UFC: Dana White confirms Michael 'Venom' Page's exit from UFC after contract ends
articles.summary: British fighter Michael 'Venom' Page is leaving the UFC after seeing out his contract, its president Dana White confirms.
articles.body:
British fighter Michael 'Venom' Page is leaving the UFC, its president Dana White has confirmed.

The 39-year-old, who is nicknamed MVP, joined MMA's top promotion in December 2023 on a six-fight contract.

He concluded that deal with an underwhelming win over Nursulton Ruziboev on Saturday amid booing from the crowd in Paris.

Page has a 5-1 record with UFC, fighting at welterweight and middleweight, but all five of those wins have come via decision and he has admitted to not delivering "what I wanted to deliver" .

Although the Londoner was keen to discuss his future with the UFC, he was removed from their rankings after Saturday's fight.

White has now added: "That was his last fight on his contract. I don't think we're signing him, no.

"What's the confusion? I think it's been pretty clear that he wasn't being re-signed and that he would be taken out of the rankings because he's no longer on the roster."

With the former Bellator fighter now a free agent, he could join a rival promotion such as the PFL or turn to boxing.

Jake Paul, co-founder of boxing and MMA company Most Valuable Promotions , has posted on X , external saying: "Think it's time to bring MVP to MVP."

Heavyweights to 'keep rolling' in Aspinall's absence

White has also said the UFC will not wait for heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall to return to action.

The British fighter is still recovering from eye injuries sustained in his fight against Cyril Gane almost a year ago.

The 33-year-old's return date is unknown but he has been cleared to return to training and says he has no plans to leave the UFC or retire.

"I mean, Tom Aspinall is hurt until we hear differently so the heavyweight division will just keep rolling," said White.

Gane claimed the interim heavyweight title with a second-round stoppage of Alex Pereira in June and the Brazilian has said he wants a rematch with the 36-year-old Frenchman .

If Aspinall remains out for the rest of 2026, White hinted Gane could take another bout in his absence.

articles.title: Conor Benn hits out at Ryan Garcia for 'bottling it' after American fails to show up for face-off in Las Vegas
articles.summary: Conor Benn will challenge Ryan Garcia for his WBC welterweight belt on Saturday night in Las Vegas; it will be the first time Benn has contested for a world title in his career and is relishing being the underdog
articles.body:
The two fighters were scheduled to meet for a media opportunity at Mandalay Bay Hotel on Tuesday, but Benn was the only one to appear.

He was joined by his father, Nigel, and, with Garcia absent, Benn jokingly squared up to his dad, who appeared to mock the WBC welterweight titleholder, telling his son: "I'm not Ryan, I turn up!"

Benn, 29, will challenge for a world title for the first time in his career on Saturday night at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, hoping to emulate the achievements of his world champion father, who won the WBO middleweight title in 1990 and the WBC super-middleweight title in 1992.

Garcia, meanwhile, is set to make the first defence of his title, but was handed a stern warning by Benn ahead of their meeting.

"Saturday can't come soon enough," Benn said on Tuesday.

"I apologise for Ryan [Garcia] doing what Ryan does and bottling it. We turn up, we're here, ready for the face-off.

"He needs to get his s*** together because come Saturday, he's in for a real, real shock."

Ben comes into this fight off the back of successive victories. His first came in November 2025, when the English fighter exacted revenge on Chris Eubank Jr, after suffering the first professional defeat of his career against his rival in April of that year.

He returned to the ring in April 2026 and outscored Regis Prograis at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to extend his fight record to 25-1.

Garcia represents a step up in opponent for Benn, with the 28-year-old American having secured his WBC welterweight belt following his dominant unanimous victory against Mario Barrios in February.

But Benn is relishing his status as the underdog, and following a protracted war of words with the American, he wants to end their verbal feud once and for all.

"I like being the underdog," Benn said. "I think I perform at my best.

"I think every single one of my fights has led me to this moment. All the pressure I've had early on in my career has prepared me for nights like those at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"It's prepared me for the noise and the drama and the chaos. So come September 12, it's nothing new, nothing different."

articles.title: Could Conor McGregor’s ACL setback and final UFC fight pave the way for a stunning BKFC homecoming at Croke Park?
articles.summary: MMA News: Conor McGregor’s UFC future has suddenly become one of the biggest questions surrounding the former two-division champion. His long-awaited return end.
articles.body: Conor McGregor’s UFC future has suddenly become one of the biggest questions surrounding the former two-division champion. His long-awaited return ended in painful fashion when a knee injury stopped his fight with Max Holloway at UFC 329. McGregor later revealed that he suffered a torn ACL, leaving him facing a lengthy recovery at an age when every comeback carries greater risk.Yet retirement does not appear to be the only road ahead. With one fight reportedly remaining on his UFC contract and BKFC president David Feldman openly interested in signing him, McGregor could have another major option waiting outside the Octagon. A potential homecoming at Dublin’s Croke Park could give the Irish superstar a dramatic new stage for what may be the final chapter of his fighting career.Conor McGregor’s injury could push his career toward a future outside the UFCMcGregor’s comeback was supposed to answer a simple question: could one of MMA’s biggest stars still compete at the highest level?Instead, the fight ended before he could provide a clear answer.The Irishman returned after a five-year absence and immediately found himself under enormous attention. His bout with Holloway was not simply another fight. It was a test of whether McGregor could still create the kind of moments that made him one of the most recognizable fighters in combat sports.The injury changed everything.McGregor attempted a flying knee early in the contest but landed awkwardly. His movement quickly became a problem, and he struggled to remain on his feet. The referee eventually stopped the contest because McGregor could not continue safely.The torn ACL also creates a difficult timeline. At 38, McGregor cannot afford to treat rehabilitation as a minor setback. A long recovery could push his next fight deep into 2027, when the UFC landscape may look completely different.Max Holloway’s own career could also move in another direction. If Holloway continues chasing opportunities at lightweight, a third meeting with McGregor may become less attractive or less practical.That leaves McGregor with a decision that goes beyond simply getting healthy.He must decide what kind of final chapter he wants.A BKFC homecoming could give Conor McGregor a completely different final actThe most intriguing possibility may be waiting outside the UFC.McGregor is already a part-owner of BKFC and has previously shown interest in bare-knuckle competition. Now BKFC president David Feldman has publicly placed an even bigger idea on the table: bringing McGregor to Croke Park for his first BKFC appearance.“Conor [McGregor] has one fight left with the UFC and then let’s see what happens but I would love to do Conor in his first BKFC fight at Croke park in front of 83,000!”That proposal carries obvious commercial appeal, but it also means something more personal.Croke Park would put McGregor back in Ireland for what could become one of the defining events of his post-UFC career. The venue has the size and history to turn a fight into a national sporting occasion. For a fighter whose rise was built partly on his ability to connect with Irish fans, the location could make the event far more meaningful than another appearance in a major American arena.There is also a clear business case for BKFC. McGregor remains one of the most recognizable names in combat sports, even after years away from consistent competition. His presence could bring attention to bare-knuckle boxing that few other fighters could match.But McGregor still has unfinished business with the UFC.One remaining fight on his contract gives the promotion a say in what happens next. Whether he completes that obligation, negotiates a different path, or eventually walks away will shape the next stage of his career.The biggest question is therefore not whether McGregor can attract another huge audience. He almost certainly can.It is whether his body will allow him to make the comeback he still wants.A return after ACL surgery would already be difficult. A return to elite MMA competition after another long layoff would make the challenge even greater. Yet McGregor has built his career around doing things that seemed unlikely.If he does return, the destination could be just as important as the opponent.The UFC may still have one final chapter to write with Conor McGregor.
